title: The quadratic formula
goal: Use x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac))/2a, and use b² − 4ac to find the number of solutions.
generalHint: Write a, b and c first. Find b² − 4ac. Then divide all of −b ± √(…) by 2a.

screens.label: RECALL
screens.title: Complete the square
screens.prompt: Look at $x^2 + 2x$. Find the number that makes it a square.

answer.correctWhy: Half of 2 is 1. The square of 1 is 1.

mistakes.reply: Use (b/2)², not b². What is half of 2, squared?
Use (b/2)². What is half of 2, squared?

screens.label: PUZZLE
screens.title: One formula for all?
screens.prompt: In lesson 4.1 the steps were the same for each equation. Only the numbers changed. Guess if one formula can solve all equations $ax^2 + bx + c = 0$.

interaction.question: Can one formula solve all of them?

options.label: Yes: the steps use only a, b and c
No: each equation needs its own method
options.reply: The steps in 4.1 did not depend on the numbers. Try them with letters.

feedback.correctWhy: The steps never used the special numbers. If you do them with the letters a, b and c, you get a formula.

screens.label: PROVE IT
screens.title: Complete the square with letters
screens.prompt: Lang takes $a \ne 0$ and starts with $\va{a}x^2 + \vb{b}x + \vc{c} = 0$. Say why each line follows. Lang uses $s = b/2a$.

steps.label: the left side is a square

wrongReasonReplies.add-c: This step moves a term to the other side. Which line has c on the right side?
wrongReasonReplies.div-a: This step divides every term by a. Which line has the x² alone?
wrongReasonReplies.add-sq: This step adds the same number to the two sides. Which number is it? Half of b/a, squared.
wrongReasonReplies.left-sq: This step writes the left side as a square. Which line shows a square on the left?
wrongReasonReplies.common: This step joins two fractions with one denominator. Which line has one fraction on the right?
wrongReasonReplies.two-roots: This step takes both square roots. Is there a square root in this step?

feedback.correctWhy: The left side is a square, and the right side has the number b² − 4ac over 4a².

screens.caption: Tap a reason to fill the orange slot.

screens.label: PROVE IT
screens.title: Solve for x
screens.prompt: Now take the last line of the proof. Suppose $b^2 - 4ac$ is 0 or positive. Say why each line follows.

steps.label: the two fractions have the same denominator
the left side is a square

wrongReasonReplies.two-roots: This step takes both square roots. Is there a square root in this step?
wrongReasonReplies.sub-b: This step moves b/2a to the right. Is there a root in this step?
wrongReasonReplies.same-den: This step joins two fractions with the same denominator. Is there a square root in this step?
wrongReasonReplies.add-sq: This step adds the same number to the two sides. Which number is it? Half of b/a, squared.
wrongReasonReplies.left-sq: This step writes the left side as a square. Which line shows a square on the left?

feedback.correctWhy: This is the quadratic formula. If b² − 4ac is negative, the right side has no real square root, so there is no real solution.

screens.caption: Tap a reason to fill the orange slot.

screens.label: NAME IT
screens.title: The quadratic formula
screens.prompt: Read it aloud like a poem: “x equals minus b, plus or minus root of b squared minus 4ac, over 2a.” Lang says to memorize it.

screens.label: EXPLORE
screens.title: How many solutions?
screens.prompt: Move the sliders. The number $b^2 - 4ac$ tells how many real solutions there are. Keep $a = 1$ and $b = 2$. Move $c$ until there is one solution.

answer.correctWhy: For a = 1 and b = 2: b² − 4ac = 4 − 4c. This is 0 when c = 1. Then x = −1 is the only solution.

mistakes.reply: b² − 4ac = 4 − 4c. For which c is it 0?
For c = −1: 4 − 4(−1) = 8. That is not 0. Try again.

screens.caption: Move c, type its value, then check.

screens.label: NAME IT
screens.title: The number b² − 4ac
screens.prompt: If $b^2 - 4ac > 0$, there are two solutions. If it is 0, there is one. If it is negative, there is no real solution.

interaction.question: The number $b^2 - 4ac$ is negative. How many real solutions are there?

options.label: One
options.reply: With a negative number under the root, the formula has no real value. How many solutions is that?

options.label: Two
options.reply: With a negative number under the root, the formula has no real value. How many solutions is that?

feedback.correctWhy: The root of a negative number is not a real number. The formula gives no real solution.

screens.label: PRACTICE · 1 OF 4
screens.title: Solve 2x² + 3x − 2 = 0
screens.prompt: Use the formula. Here $a = 2$, $b = 3$, $c = -2$. Type the solutions with a comma.

mistakes.reply: The full top, −b ± √(…), is over 2a. Divide −3 ± 5 by 4.

hints: Find $b^2 - 4ac$ first. Then divide all of $-b \pm \sqrt{\ldots}$ by $2a$.

steps.text: The number under the root is 25.
The root of 25 is 5. Divide the whole top by 4.

screens.label: PRACTICE · 2 OF 4
screens.title: Solve x² − 6x + 9 = 0
screens.prompt: Use the formula. Here $b = -6$. Type the solution.

answer.correctWhy: b² − 4ac = 36 − 36 = 0. So x = 6/2 = 3. There is only one solution.

steps.text: The root of 0 is 0. There is one solution.
A minus number times a minus number is positive.

screens.label: CHECK
screens.title: Does it have a real solution?

interaction.question: How many real solutions does $3x^2 - 2x + 1 = 0$ have?

options.label: One
options.reply: One solution needs b² − 4ac = 0. Here the number is −8.

options.label: Two
options.reply: Two solutions need b² − 4ac > 0. Here the number is −8.

feedback.correctWhy: b² − 4ac is negative, so the formula has no real value.

trap.question: True or false: if $b$ is negative, then $-b$ is negative.

options.label: True
options.reply: Try b = −6. What is −(−6)? Use N4.

feedback.correctWhy: If b = −6, then −b = 6. Minus a minus number is positive.

note.label: LANG'S NOTE
note.text: In a larger number system, the complex numbers, the formula gives solutions in all cases. A later chapter covers this.
